title: Add lightweight retrieval-adapter e2e starter + browser bindings and docsite samples
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a compact retrieval-adapter starter kit with browser-compatible bindings and integrated e2e smoke tests. Backwards-compatible; docs updated.
description:
Motivation: provide teams a compact, browser-friendly retrieval adapter that demonstrates safe embeddings usage, incremental indexing, and toolbinding patterns for small RAG workloads. This quickstart targets web-first apps where a full backend connector is not available and developers need an opinionated, lightweight flow that can be adapted to both Hosted and Private deployments.

Summary of changes: added a new quickstart under quickstarts/retrieval-adapter-lite with a minimal npm starter, a WASM-friendly indexer shim, small in-browser fetch adapter (with CORS guidelines), an example toolbinding that demonstrates document fetch -> rerank -> call LLM, and docsite samples explaining integration with Redwood API and best-practice telemetry probes. Included a compact e2e smoke test harness (Playwright) that runs against the local devserver and verifies streaming responses + tool calls.

Checklist: 
- [x] lightweight adapter implementation (JS)
- [x] WASM shim for indexing (optional locally)
- [x] browser fetch adapter + CORS doc notes
- [x] Playwright e2e smoke suite
- [x] docs site snippets and step-by-step guide
- [x] CI job added to run smoke suite on PRs

How to validate locally: checkout branch, cd quickstarts/retrieval-adapter-lite, run `yarn install && yarn dev` to start the demo server. Run `yarn e2e` to run Playwright smoke tests (requires Node 18+, headless browsers are used by CI). The quickstart includes two sample index bundles (small corpus) and a seeded API key loader (env-based) so it works with Hosted or Private endpoints.

Security and privacy notes: the browser adapter intentionally uses ephemeral session keys and recommends server-side signed short-lived tokens for production. Docsite includes a short section on recommended KMS/HSM flows for Private deployments.

Rollout: merge to main after 2 approvals, CI must pass. No migration required for existing quickstarts.

Related: references ENG-4123 for adaptive retrieval heuristics and SUP-2210 where a customer asked for a minimal browser-first demo.
